patch.value: GH-1774: parity review findings: cmd.exe-unsafe recovery commands, a claim with unreadable history reported as active, and a release after a force-claim clears the replacement holder

GH-1774 (filed 2026-11-23 from the pm-rust parity review; the Rust port reproduces each byte for byte and waits for pm-cli's decision). (1) A Windows recovery command for a tracker path containing %TRACKER% (pm --pm-path "C:\repo\%TRACKER%\pm" get item-1) is not safe to paste into cmd.exe, which expands %VAR% inside double quotes, so a pasted recovery can target another tracker; expected: escape % for cmd.exe or state that the command is for PowerShell only. pm-kjoudp (open) owns the PowerShell side of the same paste-safety contract. (2) Claiming an item whose holder's history is unreadable reports the holder as 'active under mutation_guard.stale_in_progress_hours=72' although activity could not be judged; expected: a distinct activity-unknown holder state. (3) After close, a force-claim by a second holder, then a release by the original holder clears the replacement holder (warn policy, with ownership_warning:assignee_conflict; strict policy with --force); expected: a release that ends a close releases only the holder that close ended. Duplicate check: searched cmd.exe recovery percent expansion, claim unreadable history activity unknown, release after force claim replacement holder; only pm-kjoudp overlaps (PowerShell quoting).

Windows recovery commands are paste-safe in cmd.exe (percent expansion neutralized) or explicitly declared PowerShell-only, with a rendering test for a %VAR% path; A holder whose activity cannot be judged is reported with a distinct activity-unknown state in claim refusals; Releasing as the holder a close ended never clears a replacement holder under either ownership policy
Recovery commands, holder activity and release ownership each behave as the parity review expects

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Implementation decisions (2026-11-24), one per finding. pm-rust can mirror these byte for byte.

(1) cmd.exe recovery commands. The win32 default dialect stays `cmd`; pm-kjoudp comment 2 has the full dialect decision. `quoteCmdCommandArg` keeps plain CommandLineToArgvW quoting unless the argument holds `%` or `"`. Then every cmd.exe metacharacter `( ) ! ^ " < > & |` gets a caret prefix, the quotes included, so cmd.exe never enters a quoted region. Each `%` is also followed directly by a caret (its own, or the one escaping the next metacharacter). Example: `pm --pm-path ^"C:\repo\%^TRACKER%^\pm^" get item-1`. The caret goes AFTER the percent sign on purpose. cmd.exe resolves `%NAME:a=b%` / `%NAME:~0,1%` by the text before the colon, so `^%NAME:a=b^%` (caret before) still expands NAME, but `%^NAME:a=b%^` names the undefined variable `^NAME`. A quote inside an argument triggers the caret form for a second reason: `"a\"b & calc"` flips cmd.exe's quote state at the inner quote, so the `&` would split the pasted line.

(2) Holder activity. `claim_activity.state` is `active | stale | unknown`. `unknown` exactly when the stale-work policy cannot judge the claim: history unreadable, `unproven_activity` set, or no valid activity time. The text line prints `; activity unknown under mutation_guard.stale_in_progress_hours=72 (history unreadable, last recorded activity 3h ago)` instead of `active under ...`. JSON stays additive: `stale_policy.stale` is unchanged.

(3) Release after close plus force-claim. New store primitive `CallerClaimScope` (item-store `callerClaimScope`), evaluated under the item lock only when another principal holds the item. `pm release` passes `callerClaimEndedByClose`, a forward fold over the readable stream. Each record that moves the holder principal (claim_principal, else assignee, compared as the ownership guard compares it) away from the caller ends the caller's claim; a record making the caller the holder again starts a new one. The scope applies only when the record that last ended the caller's claim is a `close`. A scoped release then ignores the ownership policy and `--force`, leaves the holder untouched and writes nothing: no history entry and no updated_at bump, so the holder's activity clock is unchanged. It returns `previous_assignee: null`, warning `release_claim_ended_by_close:<id>:<holder>` and one suggestion. The general policy stays in force in four cases: a caller whose later claim a takeover ended, a caller that never held the item, an unreadable stream, and a `--handoff`/`--pause` or ownership-release-bypass release.

value.text:
Review round 1 (PR #1779: Greptile, CodeQL, Codex gpt-6.2-sol xhigh on 1d4645f4a). Each finding was checked against the code before deciding.

Fixed:
- Legacy `/front_matter/assignee` history paths and whole-metadata writes were invisible to the close-ended fold (Greptile P1, Codex). The fold now normalizes paths with `normalizeReplayPatchPath` and applies a write or removal of the whole `/metadata` object.
- A required `claim_activity.state` broke SDK producers that build `PmCliErrorContext` (Greptile P1, Codex). The field is now optional on input and always set by pm. The text renderer derives it from the other fields when an older producer omits it.
- The fold credited a close with ending a claim even after `update --unset assignee` had left only `claim_principal` behind (Codex). It now uses the guard's rule: no non-empty assignee, no holder.
- A `--handoff`, or a `--pause` (two writes: status, then release), by the holder a close ended still moved the later holder's work (Codex). Both are now refused with `release_claim_ended_by_close` before any write. The pause pre-check runs in `runPauseTask`; the handoff is refused inside the locked callback.
- A scoped no-op could still write through implicit deferral cleanup (Codex). It now returns before `recordResolvedDeferrals`, proven with a negative control. It also skips the post-commit session-attribution write.
- POSIX double quotes let interactive bash and zsh history-expand `!` (Codex P1). Before this PR the intent `restore_with` single-quoted, so the dialect change had regressed it. `quotePosixCommandArg` now single-quotes an argument holding `!`. This resolves pm-oq893h in this PR.
- Redaction: the cmd caret form turns an encoded `%40` separator into `%^40`, which the text rule does not read as a separator. A secret under 6 characters could therefore stay visible (Codex P1). The secret and its rendered separator are now registered together. The JSON-escaped form of every shell spelling is registered too (Codex). Both are proven with negative controls.
- An evaluation clock that is not finite (`new Date(NaN)`) produced `active` with `idle_hours: NaN` (Codex P3). Such ages are now null and the state is `unknown`.
- CodeQL alerts 63, 64 and 65 (shell command from library input or environment): the POSIX corpus case now sends the rendered line to `sh -s` on stdin, so no command string reaches a shell sink.

Declined, recorded as residuals:
- (R1) A variable whose name starts with `^` (`set "^PROBE=x"`) defeats the cmd percent escape. Interactive cmd.exe has no true percent escape, and the caret-led name is the standard idiom. A user has to define such a variable on purpose.
- (R2) npm's `pm.cmd` shim re-parses `%*`. An argument holding `"` together with `^` or `&` can change in that second parse. This is the npm cmd-shim (BatBadBut) class, and the plain-quoted form had it before this PR. `pm.ps1` and a direct node entry are unaffected.
- (R3) cmd.exe with delayed expansion enabled (`cmd /v:on` or the registry key) expands `!VAR!` after carets are removed. It is off by default.
- (R4) A line break inside an argument cannot be carried through cmd.exe in any quoting. PowerShell and POSIX carry it.
- (R5) Windows PowerShell 5.1, or pwsh with `$PSNativeCommandArgumentPassing = 'Legacy'`, drops empty arguments and mangles embedded double quotes. pwsh 7.3+ in its default mode is exact, and the corpus proves that.
- (R6) After `history-compact` folds the claim and the close into a baseline, nothing records whose claim the close ended. The fold returns false and the previous ownership policy applies.
- (R7) Codex: an active claim with a workspace restore after it reports `active` with an `eligible_at`. The restore check runs only for an otherwise-stale claim. That behaviour predates this PR, and a restore can only withhold eligibility, so `active` is still truthful.

- The fold now follows replay path semantics: a whole-document replacement in either key era replaces both holder fields, and a move or copy onto a holder path makes the stream unprovable.
- A one-character secret plus `%^40` was still under one fragment long. The registry now adds up to three characters that precede the secret.
- Skipping the session attribution left the closer's workset stale, because close does not retire it. A scoped no-op retires the caller's own attribution again.
- The forced-claim hint in the refusal keeps `--pm-path`.
- Legacy evidence with a NaN idle time renders as unknown.
- CodeRabbit: the docs now qualify the `pm.cmd` second parse, the dialect tests no longer inherit PM_COMMAND_SHELL, and the redaction test checks each dialect's password spelling.
